errors.english: Noble son, the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body
errors.why: The Tibetan says the Tathāgata's body is born from all the white (virtuous) dharmas; that phrase is dropped.

fix.find: Noble son, the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body
fix.replace: Noble son, the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone, born from all virtuous qualities, is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body

errors.english: the methods for relying on the root of faith
errors.why: In context (དད་པ་བརྟན་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཐབས, དད་པའི་རྩ་བ་བརྟན་པ) this is the method for making the root of faith firm, not for relying on it.

note: A faithful rendering of the instructions on generating faith; one clause about the Dharmakāya's origin is lost.
Accurate translation of the general/individual and figurative/direct characteristics of the four truths.

errors.english: such as being like a sacrificer, being like the action of a sacrificer, being like one who is not a sacrificer, and being like that which is not the action of the continuum of a sacrifice
errors.why: མཆོད་སྦྱིན is the proper name Yajñadatta (paired with Devadatta), the agent of the example, not 'sacrificer'/'sacrifice'; the rendering runs through the whole side and garbles the argument.

fix.find: such as being like a sacrificer, being like the action of a sacrificer, being like one who is not a sacrificer, and being like that which is not the action of the continuum of a sacrifice
fix.replace: such as "like Yajñadatta," "like the action of Yajñadatta," "like what is not the agent Yajñadatta," and "like what is not the action of Yajñadatta's continuum"

errors.english: Therefore, you claim that your previous inferences do not harm our position
errors.why: The opponent says that YOUR (the Mādhyamika's) earlier inferences do not harm US (the opponent); the English makes the addressee the claimant.

fix.find: Therefore, you claim that your previous inferences do not harm our position
fix.replace: Therefore, they say, your previous inferences do not harm us

errors.english: you are not subject to the fault of having an unestablished example
errors.why: The commentator says 'I' (ཁོ་བོ) am not subject to the fault of an unestablished example.

fix.find: you are not subject to the fault of having an unestablished example
fix.replace: I am not subject to the fault of having an unestablished example

errors.english: If one asks this, the reasoning is as follows:
errors.why: The sentence continues on the next side as དེ་ནི་རིགས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ 'that is not reasonable', a rejection of the opponent's dilemma, not an introduction of reasoning.

note: Yajñadatta is read as 'sacrificer' throughout and the speakers are confused, so the opponent/commentator exchange is unreliable.

errors.english: introduces the (Samkhya) an ancient school of Hindu philosophy position
errors.why: Here 'etc.' (སོགས་པ) introduces the enumerated items, namely colour and so on (ཁ་དོག་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཉིད་དོ); nothing about the Sāṃkhya school is in view.
རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ here is the universal's (or colour's) running through all instances (anugama), as the following ཁ་དོག་རྗེས་སུ་སོང་བ shows, not logical anvaya in similar cases.

note: Sound handling of a terse pratīka-commentary on the cowness/animality universal, with two misidentified terms.

errors.english: it does not become a true logical reason
errors.why: Dignāga's point is that the similarity of the inconclusive and other pseudo-reasons is NOT thereby excluded from being a reason under the opponent's definition, since an exception cannot be read into a general rule.

fix.find: it does not become a true logical reason
fix.replace: but it is not thereby excluded from being a logical reason [under your definition]

note: Mostly accurate rendering of the critique of the Nyāya hetu definition, but the conclusion of the exception argument is inverted.

errors.english: is a plural term used to express clarity
errors.why: གསལ་བ here is the individual instances (vyakti): the plural is used because the individuals are meant.

fix.find: is a plural term used to express clarity
fix.replace: is a plural because it intends to refer to the individual instances (vyakti)

errors.english: the mental consciousness itself, which performs the connection
errors.why: མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ is rebirth-linking (pratisandhi), the mental consciousness that links to a new birth.

errors.english: the fuel (upādāna) appropriation/material cause and that which arises from the fuel—the light and the lamp
errors.why: The material cause here is the lamp and what arises from it is the light; 'fuel' misidentifies the upādāna.

errors.english: If a support makes the state of destruction occur through itself or another
errors.why: The support would cause the perishing thing to endure (གནས་བྱེད), not bring about destruction.

note: Follows the refutation of the body as support of mind, but several technical terms (vyakti, pratisandhi, upādāna) are mis-rendered.

errors.english: [note: referring to a legendary source of fire or lightning, or a specific debate example]
errors.why: Indra's head (śakramūrdhan) is the standard Pramāṇavārttika example, identified by the commentators as an anthill from which smoke-like vapour rises; the note guesses wrongly.

fix.find: [note: referring to a legendary source of fire or lightning, or a specific debate example]
fix.replace: [note: Skt. śakramūrdhan, identified by the commentators as an anthill from which smoke-like vapour rises]

errors.english: it does not deviate from being beneficial [note: being active in producing its effect]
errors.why: The Tibetan names the relation of what is assisted and what assists (upakārya-upakāraka) from the moment of arising, not simply 'being beneficial'.

note: Good grasp of the fire/smoke causation argument; the Indra's-head note is wrong and one relational term is flattened.
Faithful translation of the commentary on MMK 17.2-3 (cetanā and cetayitvā), with root verses correctly set off.

span_why: It opens by translating the previous side's 'Then what is it? It is from the object; consciousness arising without aspect is the fruit of the object', beyond the sentence that crosses the boundary.

errors.english: the mental engagement with a lamp would also become that
errors.why: The lamp(light) and attention (manaskāra) are two separate co-causes that would equally be remembered, as the commentary's སྣང་བ་ཡང་ ... དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཡིད་ལ་བྱེད་པ་ཡང་ makes clear.

fix.find: the mental engagement with a lamp would also become that
fix.replace: the lamp [light] and mental engagement would also become that

errors.english: could a person possibly perceive that object as possessing a form?
errors.why: What the person may mistakenly take as having the object's aspect is the aspectless experienced cognition, not the object.

note: The memory argument is broadly followed, but it re-translates the previous side and merges light and attention into one.

errors.english: like the lord of the immortals [note: Indra, king of the gods] and the teacher of the gods [note: Bṛhaspati, preceptor of the gods] and
errors.why: The phrase most likely names one figure, the guru of the lord of the immortals (Bṛhaspati), not Indra and Bṛhaspati as two comparanda.

note: A fluent and faithful rendering of the close of the Ṛṣi-jātaka and the opening of the next story.
